title: The six layers of an embedded Linux board

steps.title: Six layers, always started in this order
steps.body:
Whatever the vendor calls them, every board boots through the same six layers.

This walkthrough takes them one at a time. Use **→** and **←**, or press **space** to play.

steps.title: 1 · Boot ROM: the part you can never change
steps.body:
Code inside the chip, fixed at the factory. It reads the **boot-mode switch**, looks for the next stage on SD, eMMC, QSPI or USB and loads it into on-chip RAM.

It decides **where your first loader must sit** on the storage, which is why every board's image layout is different.

steps.title: 2 · First-stage firmware and the secure world
steps.body:
DRAM does not work at power-on: this layer **trains it**, from on-chip RAM. It then installs the **secure monitor** (TF-A, at the highest privilege level) and optionally a trusted OS (OP-TEE).

When this layer is wrong the board prints **nothing at all**.

steps.title: 3 · Bootloader: U-Boot or UEFI
steps.body: The first stage with a prompt. It picks a kernel and a **device tree**, builds the kernel command line (`console=`, `root=`) and jumps. Most boot problems are fixed here, from the serial console, without re-flashing.

steps.title: 4 · Kernel and device tree
steps.body: Linux, plus the **device tree**: a data file that tells it which hardware exists and where, because an SoC's peripherals cannot be discovered like PCI devices. Most board customization happens at this layer.

steps.title: 5 · Root filesystem
steps.body: Everything in `/`: init, shell, libraries, packages. This is the layer that is *just Linux*. Debian, Alpine, a vendor image or a Yocto build all fit here.

steps.title: 6 · Your application
steps.body: The reason the board exists, and the only layer that changes weekly. Everything below it should change as rarely as possible, which is why this repository makes layers 2 to 5 **reproducible**.

steps.title: How this repository maps onto the layers
steps.body: `./build.sh uboot` builds layers 2 and 3, `kernel` layer 4, `rootfs` layer 5, and `image` glues 1 to 5 into one flashable artifact.
